feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=9.$ Find $P(x).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=9,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =9{(x-(-\frac{2}{3}))}^{2} \\  & =9{(x+\frac{2}{3})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(x+\frac{2}{3})}^{2} & =9({x}^{2}+\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{4}{9}) \\  & =9{x}^{2}+12x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=9{x}^{2}+12x+4.$
